purpose: Keep the kernel/vendor base, Linux build essentials, Python 3 control plane, and Godot 4 game source in separately bounded modules. Apply the shared four-tier escalation policy to any module or declared cross-module scope.

sourceModules.title: Canonical kernel and machine/vendor capsule
sourceModules.localDelta: smallest device configuration, compatibility patch, and separately isolated Samsung/vendor backend or SDK adapters

sourceModules.title: Linux build essentials
sourceModules.purpose: pinned Linux/Ubuntu build tools and reproducible system toolchain used to build and verify the source modules
sourceModules.boundary: toolchain and system dependencies are versioned separately from application source

sourceModules.title: Python 3 control plane
sourceModules.purpose: LuHm/Hydra service and API-broker source with stable contracts to platform adapters and clients
sourceModules.boundary: Python services own control-plane behavior; they do not vendor kernel or game-engine implementation

sourceModules.title: Godot 4 video-game source
sourceModules.purpose: gameplay, scenes, assets, and game-client source for Project Hydra
sourceModules.boundary: game code calls stable service interfaces and does not absorb platform/vendor authority

escalation.application: the four escalation tiers can audit any one module or an explicitly declared cross-module scope
escalation.separationLaw: module order defines source boundaries; escalation tier defines operational audit depth; tier increase changes focus and proof maturity, not authority
escalation.scopeLaw: every tier preserves taskId/sourceRef/scopeId and stops at unresolved red or missing authority

matrixLaw: four source modules by four operational escalation tiers; no one-to-one assignment of module order to escalation authority
